summary: A series of community wellness workshops, Nutrition and Balanced Diet Essentials for Every Age, began in fall 2023 to teach age-specific dietary guidelines to families. Weekly sessions led by different nutrition professionals covered children, teens, adults, middle age, seniors, family meal planning, and barriers to healthy eating. The core principles (whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fruits, vegetables) stay constant, while specific needs change with life stage.
one_line: A fall 2023 community workshop series taught age-tailored nutrition, from children to seniors, led by local dietitians and nutritionists.
key_facts: The Nutrition and Balanced Diet Essentials for Every Age workshop series launched in fall 2023, after September 1st, 2023, to educate the community about age-specific dietary guidelines.
Local nutritionist Emily Harris opened the series on Saturday, September 10, 2023, saying "Nutrition should be family-centric, a legacy passed down to ensure longevity and vitality."
The core principles of a balanced diet stay relatively constant across ages: whole grains, lean proteins, healthy fats, fruits, and vegetables.
Pediatric dietitian Joshua Klein spoke on September 17th, recommending calcium-rich foods for bone development and iron-rich sources to aid cognitive advancement in children.
A parent's guide distributed at Joshua Klein's workshop offers creative recipes for choosy eaters.

Local dietician Sarah Johnson spoke on September 24 about teen nutrition, stressing protein, iron, and calcium to support a second wave of growth and encouraging teens to take part in meal planning and preparation.
Nutritionist Mark Lee's October 1st workshop addressed adults' slowing metabolism, stressing fiber-rich foods and controlled portions, saying "This isn't about dieting."
Dietician Sandra Choi presented on October 8th about antioxidants and omega-3 fatty acids for heart and brain health in middle age, and ran an interactive Q&A debunking nutrition myths.

Geriatric nutrition expert David Thompson spoke on October 15th about senior challenges such as tooth loss and reduced digestive function, advising easy-to-chew foods rich in B12 and fortified with vitamin D.
Family nutrition consultant Maria Gonzales led the penultimate workshop on October 22nd, with a cooking demo showing how one meal can be adapted for all age groups.
Health coach Robert Foster closed the series on October 29th on barriers like time scarcity and processed foods, with the mantra "Small, steady changes lead to significant lifelong benefits."
